facts.raw_span: A female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of vesicles with an erythematous base, along with the histopathological findings of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods, is consistent with bacillary angiomatosis, a disease caused by Bartonella henselae.

The patient's history of fever, neutropenia, and indwelling catheter, along with the presence of lesions in the liver and brain, could be consistent with disseminated cat-scratch disease, a condition caused by Bartonella henselae.

The patient's presentation of fever and neutropenia, along with the presence of an indwelling catheter, is consistent with neutropenic sepsis, a life-threatening condition that requires prompt treatment.

The patient's history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and recent reinduction chemotherapy, along with the presence of lesions in the liver and brain, could be consistent with relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
It explains the presence of vesicles with an erythematous base and the microscopic findings of focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli.

rationales.F05: Vesicles with an erythematous base are consistent with Bacillary angiomatosis and Ecthyma gangrenosum
rationales.F06: Filamentous bacilli with septa are characteristic of Bacillary angiomatosis
rationales.F07: Gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis are consistent with Bacillary angiomatosis
rationales.F10: Lesions in the liver and brain are consistent with disseminated infection, such as Bacillary angiomatosis or Disseminated cat-scratch disease

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an indwelling catheter, neutropenia, and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, along with the clinical presentation of vesicles with an erythematous base, are highly suggestive of Ecthyma gangrenosum, a condition often associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in immunocompromised patients.
